questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct in relation to Western Ghats? 1. The Western Ghats are the main reason for the monsoon rain in the western coast of India. 2. statements.text: The Western Ghats are the main reason for the monsoon rain in the western coast of India.
Western Ghats are locally known as Sahyadri in Tamil Nadu and Nilgiri hills in Telangana.
Heights of the Western Ghats decrease from north to south.

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats block rain-bearing winds which cause rainfall on the western slopes. Whereas, South-West monsoon moves parallel to the Eastern Ghats, which cause less rainfall, because in the Eastern Ghats they are unable to block moisture laden winds. The Western Ghats lies in rain-fed area of the Arabian Sea branch of the South-West Monsoon whereas Eastern Ghats lies in the rain shadow area of the Arabian sea branch of the South-West Monsoon. Western Ghats are known as Sahyadri in Maharashtra. Height of Western Ghats increases from North to South.

questions.question: The Palk strait lies between:

options.text: Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Khambhat
Gulf of Mannar and Bay of Bengal

questions.explanation: The Palk Strait is a strait between the Tamil Nadu state of India and the Jaffna District of the Northern Province of the island nation of Sri Lanka. It connects the Bay of Bengal in the northeast with Palk Strait in the southwest. Palk strait is situated at its southern end with a chain of low islands and reef shoals that are collectively called Adam's Bridge. This chain extends between Dhanushkodi on Pamban Island (also known as Rameswaram Island) in Tamil Nadu and Mannar Island in Sri Lanka. The island of Rameswaram is linked to the Indian mainland by the Pamban Bridge.
